text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock rose 0.31% today to close at $388.90, continuing a strong two-week rally of 7.8%. The gains reflect tightening global refinery capacity: diesel prices hit record highs this week as Ukraine's strikes on Russian refineries and Iran sanctions have knocked major suppliers offline, while U.S. refineries are running at 98% capacity with constrained product storage. For a major U.S. refiner like Marathon, tight markets and elevated fuel prices directly boost margins on the fuel they produce and sell.

The broader geopolitical backdrop supports this rally. News of a Trump administration deal with Venezuela, combined with escalating sanctions on Iran and Russia's refining sector, is removing crude oil supplies and refining capacity from global markets at the same time — pushing crude prices up to $91 domestically and $96 globally. This kind of supply disruption in refining typically translates into stronger profits for U.S. refiners positioned to fill the gap.
